Every Y Combinator company · 2005 – 2026

The YC Denominator exitseveryone

Success stories are the numerator. This page counts the denominator: every company YC has funded, batch by batch, including the ones that died quietly. For each one it shows what happened, how long it took and when they raised money. Pick what a decent exit means to you; every chart updates.

The odds, measured on mature batches

How the odds build up, year by year after YC

Cumulative share of a cohort that has reached each outcome N years after its batch started. Young batches count only for the years they have lived through. This is a competing-risks (Aalen–Johansen) estimate, so it doesn't assume every live company will eventually exit.

One bar per batch, split by what happened to each company. Older batches are mostly settled. In recent ones, most companies are still too young for any outcome. Click a batch to see its companies below.

When exits happen, and how big they are

Each dot is one exit. It's placed by years from batch start to the deal and by deal value on a log scale. Filled dots are disclosed or credibly reported values. Hollow dots are estimated size buckets (under $10M, $10–50M and so on), spread across their bucket. The dashed line marks your threshold.

How far companies get with funding

Of every company in a batch era, the share that reached each funding milestone, and then a decent exit. 2026 batches are left out because they're too new. The 2022–25 companies are still mid-journey, so their bars will keep growing.

Company trajectories

Every company in a batch on its own timeline, from batch start to today. Dots are funding rounds, sized by amount. ◆ marks an exit, ✕ a shutdown. Hover or click a row to see what happened and the sources.

Select a company to see its story, funding rounds and sources.

What founders actually take home

An exit's value isn't founder money. This estimates each founder's share after dilution and after investors are paid back, spread over the years they spent on the company. It covers every company from 2005–2019 batches, including the ones that died. Move the assumptions to see how much they matter.
